title: PR signal mapping scratch
content:
TL;DR:
Quick, messy brain-dump for mapping reviewer signals -> review actions. Goal: make a 5-minute triage rubric reviewers can run through, plus a short backlog of small refactors we can ship post-merge. Mostly personal notes; share and iterate.

Context / motivation:
- We get too many PRs that look small but have latent risk (tests that flake, implicit behavior changes, perf regressions).
- Need a compact signal -> action mapping for quick reviewers and for on-call SREs who triage post-merge regressions.
- This is intentionally lightweight: prioritize cheap mitigations (smoke tests, canaries, short followups) instead of large redesigns during review.

Quick checklist (5–7 checks, run in ~5m):
1) Surface change magnitude: lines + files + top-level deps changed. If >400LOC or >8 files: mark as "large-change", request more context and run local integration smoke.
2) Behavioral flag: does this touch user-facing path, DB schema, auth, or metrics emitters? If yes -> require a short PR description section: "Behavioral impact" with example request/response.
3) Test signal: new tests added? If yes, check for determinism (no sleeps, no time.Now stubs without control). If no tests added and change touches logic -> request one test or a smoke run note.
4) Perf/latency risk: any loops over tokens / batch sizes / I/O? If yes -> run local perf snapshot (script ./dev/perf-check.sh) or request a benchmark.
5) Observability: does it include metrics or logs for critical paths? If not and change affects routing/batching/cache, ask for minimal metric or a TODO ticket.
6) Migration surface: schema/contract change? Ensure migration plan or compatibility guard is included.
7) Rollout plan: if change affects latency or costs, require a canary plan + rollback trigger (e.g., revert threshold or quick-fallback route).

Heuristic signal mapping (when you see X -> do Y):
- Many small file renames + reorganize: low behavioral risk, but high merge pain -> recommend staged merge (split if possible) and add a follow-up to restore git history mapping.
- Addition of a cache with no eviction policy described: medium-high risk -> ask for eviction rationale and a fallout plan; recommend a short load test.
- Changes touching kv-cache logic (hot path): treat as high risk -> require bench + snapshot of tail latency on canary.
- PRs that only tweak log levels or error text: low risk; push a micro patch if tests pass, but ask for a changelog note if customer-facing.
- New third-party dependency: require security/oss approval link and a size/footprint estimate.

Refactor ideas (short items we can do as follow-ups):
- Small adapter layer for batcher impls: unify the batching interface so reviewer can reason about routing changes in one place. Priority: low-medium. (ENG-2143 as umbrella).
- Move common perf checks into a pre-merge runner: lightweight script that runs module-level tokenized calls with 2 sizes (small/large). Hook into local dev flow. Priority: medium.
- Standardize a 3-line PR metadata template (behavioral-impact, rollout, perf-impacted). Add a lint that warns if missing. Priority: high.
- Add a "quick metric" library helper that auto-instruments latency for public handler wrappers with a one-line opt-in. Reduces reviewer burden to ask for metrics. Priority: medium.

Follow-ups and tickets to create (short):
- TICKET: add-pr-template-lint (add metadata template + CI warning) -> owner: Ibrahim / due: 2025-03-01
- TICKET: bench-script-premerge (dev/perf-check.sh cleanup + README) -> owner: Ravi -> due: 2025-03-15
- TICKET: kv-cache-canary-playbook (how to run, metrics to monitor, rollback steps) -> owner: Aisha -> due: 2025-03-08

Example review comments (copyable):
- "Can you add a short `Behavioral impact` section showing an example request/response and the expected change? This helps reviewers and on-call."
- "Heads up: this touches kv-cache hot path. Can you include a bench snapshot or run `./dev/perf-check.sh` and paste results? If bench is costly, please add a canary plan."
- "Please add a brief rollback / canary note in the PR description (what metric to watch and threshold). If you prefer, open a follow-up ticket and annotate it here."

Open questions / edge cases to think about:
- How small is "small enough" to not need a perf bench? (heuristic: if change touches token-level loops or batching internals, bench is required).
- When is it acceptable to push a partial implementation without full metrics? (Answer: only for internal-only feature flags behind a toggle with default off).
- Should "quick metric" helper auto-instrument be opt-in or opt-out? Lean opt-in for safety, but dev UX matters.

Notes-to-self (later):
- Run PR-lint experiment on a sample of 200 PRs to see how many would have required the extra metadata; use that to push template enforcement.
- Draft a 1-page "review quick rubric" card (printable) for on-call SREs.

Misc links & commands:
- Local perf script: ./dev/perf-check.sh (TODO: consolidate args)
- Canary verification checklist (draft): confluence://pages/Canary-Checklist
- Reference PR with good metadata: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4821 (see Behavioral impact section)

Small wins to push asap:
- Ask teams to include a single line in PR title with impacted surface: [routing] [batcher] [kv-cache] etc. Tagging encourages reviewer focus.
- Add "metrics TODO" label to GitHub; auto-add when PR touches known paths (simple path map in a small GitHub Action).

End of dump. This is my working draft — will tidy into a small playbook once we validate with a few reviewers.

Quick snapshot of tags to use in PR comments:
- [perf-check-required]
- [behavioral-impact-missing]
- [canary-needed]

-- Ibrahim
